summary: A forest kund and cave on Anjani hill held locally as Hanuman's birthplace — a short trek into Dang's Ramayana geography.
description:
Anjan Kund extends Dang's Ramayana map beyond the Shabari sites: a spring-fed kund and cave shrine on Anjani Parvat, held in local tradition to be where Anjani gave birth to Hanuman. The claim is contested by other regions of India — as Hanuman birthplaces famously are — but Dang's version comes with an atmospheric setting: forest slopes, a rock pool that holds water into the dry months, and a cave where pilgrims leave sindoor and coconuts.

Reaching it is a small adventure — a rough approach road and then a forest footpath climb of twenty to forty minutes depending on the route taken. Hanuman Jayanti and Shravan Saturdays bring local pilgrim traffic; most other days you will have the hillside to yourself apart from herders.

Combine it with the Shabari Dham circuit for a half-day of Dang's sacred geography. Facilities are effectively nil — water, footwear and daylight margins are your responsibility.
highlights: Dang's claimed Hanuman birthplace — kund and cave shrine
history_legend: Local tradition holds Anjani Parvat as the site where Anjani bore Hanuman; the kund is her bathing pool in the telling. Other regions — from Anjaneri near Nashik to sites in Karnataka — hold rival claims. Dang's version belongs to the same living Ramayana geography as Shabari Dham and Pampa Sarovar.

modes.road: Village roads off the Ahwa–Subir corridor to the trailhead; ask locally — signage is thin

access.last_mile: 20–40 min forest footpath climb from the road end
access.road_condition: Rough village tar and dirt for the final approach

visit.notes: Open site; on Hanuman Jayanti expect a village-fair atmosphere.

seasonality.notes: Post-monsoon through winter for footing and views; the path is slick in active rain.

experience.photography_notes: The kund pool and cave mouth shoot best mid-morning when light reaches the slope.

amenities.food: None — carry everything; nearest food at Subir/Ahwa
amenities.guides: A local from the base village is worth the small fee — paths braid

warnings: Do not attempt the wet-rock sections around the kund in monsoon
Carry water and keep daylight margin for the descent

tips: Fold into the Shabari Dham–Pampa Sarovar circuit for a sacred-geography half day
Ask directions in Subir rather than trusting maps blindly — the trailhead is unsigned

faqs.q: Is this the actual birthplace of Hanuman?
faqs.a: It is Dang's traditional claim; Anjaneri near Nashik and several other sites hold rival ones. Visit it as living local devotion in a beautiful setting rather than settled fact.
